claim: In 2021, there were an estimated 619,000 deaths due to malaria, with children under 5 accounting for 77% of these.
source: In 2021, there were an estimated 619,000 deaths due to malaria, with children under 5 accounting for 77% of these (WHO, 2022).
evidence: The claim cites WHO 2022 as the source for these statistics.

claim: Plasmodium falciparum causes the greatest disease burden and most severe outcomes.
source: Plasmodium falciparum causes the greatest disease burden and most severe outcomes, but our efforts to combat the disease are challenged by its complex life cycle and its sophisticated immune evasion strategies.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction without specific data provided in this manuscript.

claim: About 60 polymorphic var genes per parasite genome encode different PfEMP1 variants.
source: About 60 polymorphic var genes per parasite genome encode different PfEMP1 variants, which are exported to the surface of parasite-infected erythrocytes, where they mediate cytoadherence to host endothelial cells (Leech et al., 1984; Su et al., 1995; Smith et al., 1995; Baruch et al., 1995; Rask et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Var genes are expressed in a mutually exclusive pattern, resulting in each parasite expressing only one var gene at a time.
source: Var genes are expressed in a mutually exclusive pattern, resulting in each parasite expressing only one var gene, and therefore one PfEMP1 protein, at a time (Scherf et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim cites Scherf et al., 1998 as the source.

claim: Var genes can be classified into four categories (A, B, C, and E) according to their chromosomal location, transcriptional direction, type of 5'-upstream sequence, and encoded protein domains.
source: Despite their sequence polymorphism, var genes could be classified into four categories (A, B, C, and E) according to their chromosomal location, transcriptional direction, type of 5'-upstream sequence (UPSA–E), and encoded protein domains with associated binding phenotype (Figure 1; Lavstsen et al., 2003; Kraemer and Smith, 2003; Kyes et al., 2007; Rask et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations and references Figure 1 which illustrates the classification.

claim: PfEMP1 proteins with CIDRα1 domains bind endothelial protein C receptor (EPCR).
source: The PfEMP1 family divides into three main groups based on the receptor specificity of the N-terminal CIDR domain: (i) PfEMP1 proteins with CIDRα1 domains bind endothelial protein C receptor (EPCR), while (ii) PfEMP1 proteins with CIDRα2–6 domains bind CD36 and (iii) the atypical VAR2CSA PfEMP1 proteins bind placental chondroitin sulphate A (CSA) (Salanti et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim cites Salanti et al., 2004 as the source.

claim: PfEMP1 proteins with CIDRα2–6 domains bind CD36.
source: The PfEMP1 family divides into three main groups based on the receptor specificity of the N-terminal CIDR domain: (i) PfEMP1 proteins with CIDRα1 domains bind endothelial protein C receptor (EPCR), while (ii) PfEMP1 proteins with CIDRα2–6 domains bind CD36 and (iii) the atypical VAR2CSA PfEMP1 proteins bind placental chondroitin sulphate A (CSA) (Salanti et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim cites Salanti et al., 2004 as the source.

claim: VAR2CSA PfEMP1 proteins bind placental chondroitin sulphate A (CSA).
source: The PfEMP1 family divides into three main groups based on the receptor specificity of the N-terminal CIDR domain: (i) PfEMP1 proteins with CIDRα1 domains bind endothelial protein C receptor (EPCR), while (ii) PfEMP1 proteins with CIDRα2–6 domains bind CD36 and (iii) the atypical VAR2CSA PfEMP1 proteins bind placental chondroitin sulphate A (CSA) (Salanti et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim cites Salanti et al., 2004 as the source.

claim: Pregnancy-associated malaria is linked to parasites expressing VAR2CSA.
source: Pregnancy-associated malaria is linked to parasites expressing VAR2CSA, whereas parasites expressing EPCR-binding PfEMP1 are linked to severe malaria and parasites expressing CD36-binding PfEMP1 are linked to uncomplicated malaria (Turner et al., 2013; Lavstsen et al., 2012; Avril et al., 2012; Claessens et al., 2012; Tonkin-Hill et al., 2018; Wichers et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Parasites expressing EPCR-binding PfEMP1 are linked to severe malaria.
source: Pregnancy-associated malaria is linked to parasites expressing VAR2CSA, whereas parasites expressing EPCR-binding PfEMP1 are linked to severe malaria and parasites expressing CD36-binding PfEMP1 are linked to uncomplicated malaria (Turner et al., 2013; Lavstsen et al., 2012; Avril et al., 2012; Claessens et al., 2012; Tonkin-Hill et al., 2018; Wichers et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Parasites expressing CD36-binding PfEMP1 are linked to uncomplicated malaria.
source: Pregnancy-associated malaria is linked to parasites expressing VAR2CSA, whereas parasites expressing EPCR-binding PfEMP1 are linked to severe malaria and parasites expressing CD36-binding PfEMP1 are linked to uncomplicated malaria (Turner et al., 2013; Lavstsen et al., 2012; Avril et al., 2012; Claessens et al., 2012; Tonkin-Hill et al., 2018; Wichers et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The new whole transcript approach produced the fewest transcripts, but of greater length than the domain approach and the original approach.
source: The whole transcript approach produced the fewest transcripts, but of greater length than the domain approach and the original approach (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim references Figure 2—figure supplement 2 which shows the comparison data.

claim: The whole transcript approach returned the largest N50 score, more than doubling the N50 of the original approach.
source: The whole transcript approach also returned the largest N50 score (more than doubling the N50 of the original approach), which means that it was the most contiguous assembly produced.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison data presented in the manuscript.

claim: With the new whole transcript method, there was a significant decrease (2 vs 336) in clearly misassembled transcripts.
source: Remarkably, with the new whole transcript method, we observed a significant decrease (2 vs 336) in clearly misassembled transcripts with, for example, an N-terminal domain at an internal position.
evidence: The claim provides specific numerical comparison data.

claim: The original approach failed to assemble the N-terminal region in 58% of the samples, compared to just 4% in the new approach.
source: The original approach failed to assemble the N-terminal region in 58% of the samples, compared to just 4% in the new approach with assembly consistently achieved with an accuracy >90%.
evidence: The claim provides specific percentage comparison data.

claim: Assembly completeness of the lowly expressed var genes increased fivefold using the new approach.
source: Assembly completeness of the lowly expressed var genes increased fivefold using the new approach.
evidence: The claim provides a specific quantitative comparison.

claim: Of the 32 clinical isolates of P. falciparum from the German traveller dataset, 13 underwent one replication cycle of in vitro culture, 10 of these underwent a second generation and one underwent a third generation.
source: Of the 32 clinical isolates of P. falciparum from the German traveller dataset, 13 underwent one replication cycle of in vitro culture, 10 of these underwent a second generation and one underwent a third generation (Table 3).
evidence: The claim references Table 3 which provides the sample details.

claim: Most (9/13, 69%) isolates entering culture had a single MSP1 genotype, indicative of monoclonal infections.
source: Most (9/13, 69%) isolates entering culture had a single MSP1 genotype, indicative of monoclonal infections.
evidence: The claim provides specific numerical data from the study.

claim: A change in the dominant var gene being expressed through culture was observed in isolates from 3 of 13 (23%) patients (#6, #17, and #26).
source: However, we observed a change in the dominant var gene being expressed through culture in isolates from 3 of 13 (23%) patients (#6, #17, and #26).
evidence: The claim provides specific numerical data from the analysis.

claim: In patient #26, there was a switch from a dominant group A var gene to a group B and C var gene.
source: Interestingly, in patient #26 we observed a switch from a dominant group A var gene to a group B and C var gene.
evidence: The claim describes a specific observation from the data analysis.

claim: var2csa was significantly differentially expressed between generation 1 and generation 2 parasites (padj = 0.029, paired Wilcoxon test).
source: We observed no significant differences in the expression of conserved var gene variants, var1-IT (padj = 0.61, paired Wilcoxon test), var1-3D7 (padj = 0.93, paired Wilcoxon test), and var2csa (padj = 0.54, paired Wilcoxon test) between paired ex vivo and generation 1 parasites, but var2csa was significantly differentially expressed between generation 1 and generation 2 parasites (padj = 0.029, paired Wilcoxon test) (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim provides statistical test results and references a figure.

claim: A single domain, CIDRα2.5 associated with B-type PfEMP1 proteins and CD36 binding, was significantly differentially expressed in the generation 1 vs ex vivo comparison.
source: However, in the pooled comparison of the generation 1 vs ex vivo of all isolates, a single domain was significantly differentially expressed, CIDRα2.5 associated with B-type PfEMP1 proteins and CD36 binding (Figure 5b).
evidence: The claim references Figure 5b which shows the differential expression analysis results.

claim: No significant changes were found in total group A or group B and C var gene expression levels.
source: In both approaches, DBLα and NTS, we found no significant changes in total group A or group B and C var gene expression levels (Figure 6).
evidence: The claim references Figure 6 which shows the analysis results.

claim: 920 core genes (19% of the core transcriptome) were found to be differentially expressed between ex vivo and generation 1 samples.
source: In total, 920 core genes (19% of the core transcriptome) were found to be differentially expressed after adjusting for life cycle stages using the mixture model approach between ex vivo and generation 1 samples (Supplementary file 6).
evidence: The claim provides specific numerical data from the differential expression analysis.

claim: The majority of differentially expressed core genes were upregulated, indicating a substantial transcriptional change during the first cycle of in vitro cultivation.
source: The majority were upregulated, indicating a substantial transcriptional change during the first cycle of in vitro cultivation (Figure 7b).
evidence: The claim references Figure 7b which shows the volcano plot of differential expression.

claim: Eight AP2 transcription factors were upregulated in generation 1.
source: We observed eight AP2 transcription factors upregulated in generation 1 (PF3D7_0404100/AP2-SP2, PF3D7_0604100/SIP2, PF3D7_0611200/AP2-EXP2, PF3D7_0613800, PF3D7_0802100/AP2-LT, PF3D7_1143100/AP2-O, PF3D7_1239200, PF3D7_1456000/AP2-HC) with no AP2 transcription factors found to be downregulated in generation 1.
evidence: The claim provides specific gene identifiers from the analysis.

claim: 206 core genes were significantly upregulated in naïve patients compared to pre-exposed patients when using ex vivo samples.
source: Interestingly, when using the ex vivo samples, we observed 206 core genes significantly upregulated in naïve patients compared to pre-exposed patients (Figure 7—figure supplement 3a).
evidence: The claim references Figure 7—figure supplement 3a which shows the differential expression results.

claim: No differentially expressed genes were observed in the naïve vs pre-exposed analysis of the paired generation 1 samples.
source: Conversely, we observed no differentially expressed genes in the naïve vs pre-exposed analysis of the paired generation 1 samples (Figure 7—figure supplement 3b).
evidence: The claim references Figure 7—figure supplement 3b which shows the analysis results.

claim: The concordance of different var profiling approaches increased using the new approach by 13%, when compared to the original approach (96% in the whole transcript approach compared to 83% in Wichers et al., 2021).
source: Concordance in the different var expression profiling approaches (RNA-sequencing and DBLα-tag) on ex vivo samples increased using the new approach by 13%, when compared to the original approach (96% in the whole transcript approach compared to 83% in Wichers et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim provides specific percentage comparison data.

claim: A median of 96% (IQR: 93–100%) of all unique DBLα-tag sequences detected with >10 reads were found in the RNA-sequencing approach.
source: Overall, we found a high agreement between the detected DBLα-tag sequences and the de novo assembled var transcripts. A median of 96% (IQR: 93–100%) of all unique DBLα-tag sequences detected with >10 reads were found in the RNA-sequencing approach.
evidence: The claim provides specific statistical data from the validation analysis.

claim: A median of 77.4% (IQR: 61–88%) of the upper 75th percentile of the assembled DBLα domains were found in the DBLα-tag approach.
source: A median of 77.4% (IQR: 61–88%) of the upper 75th percentile of the assembled DBLα domains were found in the DBLα-tag approach.
evidence: The claim provides specific statistical data from the validation analysis.

claim: A median of 85% of the DBLα annotations and 73% of the DBLα-CIDR domain annotations identified using the DBLα-tag approach were found in the RNA-sequencing approach.
source: A median of 85% of the DBLα annotations and 73% of the DBLα-CIDR domain annotations, respectively, identified using the DBLα-tag approach were found in the RNA-sequencing approach.
evidence: The claim provides specific percentage data from the validation analysis.

claim: The new approach allows for var transcript reconstruction across a range of expression levels.
source: The new approach allows for var transcript reconstruction across a range of expression levels, which is required when characterising var transcripts from multi-clonal infections.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of the new method based on the validation results.

claim: The new approach is not limited by parasite stage and was able to assemble the whole var transcript, in a single contig, at later stages in the P. falciparum 3D7 intra-erythrocytic cycle.
source: Biases towards certain parasite stages have been observed in non-severe and severe malaria cases, so it is valuable to assemble the var transcripts from different life cycle stages (Tonkin-Hill et al., 2018). Our new approach is not limited by parasite stage. It was able to assemble the whole var transcript, in a single contig, at later stages in the P. falciparum 3D7 intra-erythrocytic cycle, something previously unachievable.
evidence: The claim is supported by the validation results on the 3D7 time course dataset.

claim: Modest but unpredictable var gene switching and convergence towards var2csa were observed in culture.
source: Modest but unpredictable var gene switching and convergence towards var2csa were observed in culture, along with differential expression of 19% of the core transcriptome between paired ex vivo and generation 1 samples.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main findings from the analysis.

claim: Our results cast doubt on the validity of the common practice of using short-term cultured parasites to make inferences about in vivo phenotype and behaviour.
source: Our results cast doubt on the validity of the common practice of using short-term cultured parasites to make inferences about in vivo phenotype and behaviour.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: One cycle of cultivation shifts the core transcriptomes of parasites to be more alike each other, diminishing inferences about parasite biology in vivo.
source: Taken together with the preceding findings, this suggests one cycle of cultivation shifts the core transcriptomes of parasites to be more alike each other, diminishing inferences about parasite biology in vivo.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the differential expression analysis results.

claim: The N-terminal region is known to contribute to the adhesion phenotypes of most PfEMP1 proteins.
source: This was particularly apparent in the N-terminal region, which has often been poorly characterised by existing approaches. The original approach failed to assemble the N-terminal region in 58% of the samples, compared to just 4% in the new approach with assembly consistently achieved with an accuracy >90%. This is important because the N-terminal region is known to contribute to the adhesion phenotypes of most PfEMP1 proteins.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about PfEMP1 protein function.

claim: Switching to var2csa has been shown to be favourable and is suggested to be the default var gene upon perturbation to var-specific heterochromatin.
source: It has previously been suggested that long-term cultured parasites converge to expressing var2csa, but our findings suggest this begins within two cycles of cultivation (Zhang et al., 2022; Mok et al., 2008). Switching to var2csa has been shown to be favourable and is suggested to be the default var gene upon perturbation to var-specific heterochromatin (Ukaegbu et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim cites Ukaegbu et al., 2015 as the source.

claim: var2csa has a unique role in var gene switching and is the dominant 'sink node'.
source: These studies also suggested that var2csa has a unique role in var gene switching and our results are consistent with the role of var2csa as the dominant 'sink node' (Zhang et al., 2022; Ukaegbu et al., 2015; Ukaegbu et al., 2014; Mok et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Short-term culture can result in unpredictable var gene expression.
source: Almost a quarter of samples in our analysis showed more pronounced and unpredictable changes. In these individuals, the dominant var gene being expressed changed within one cycle of cultivation. This implies that short-term culture can result in unpredictable var gene expression as observed previously using a semi-quantitative RT-PCR approach (Bachmann et al., 2011) and that one would need to confirm in vivo expression matches in vitro expression.
evidence: The claim is based on the data analysis results and cites a previous study.

claim: There is probably not a selection event occurring during culture but may represent a loss of selection that is present in vivo.
source: We observed no generalised pattern of up- or downregulation of specific var groups following transition to culture. This implies that there is probably not a selection event occurring during culture but may represent a loss of selection that is present in vivo.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the var group expression analysis results.

claim: The impact of short-term culture was the most apparent at the var transcript level and became less clear at the var domain, var type and global var gene expression level.
source: Generally, there was a high consensus between all levels of var gene analysis and changes observed during short-term in vitro cultivation. However, the impact of short-term culture was the most apparent at the var transcript level and became less clear at the var domain, var type and global var gene expression level.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the multi-level analysis results.

claim: The culture conditions may temporarily dysregulate stage-specific expression patterns or result in the parasites undergoing a rapid adaptation response.
source: We observed that genes with functions unrelated to ring-stage parasites were among those most significantly expressed in the generation 1 vs ex vivo analysis, suggesting the culture conditions may temporarily dysregulate stage-specific expression patterns or result in the parasites undergoing a rapid adaptation response (Andreadaki et al., 2020; Beeson et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the differential expression results, supported by citations.

claim: Short-term cultured parasites might be transcriptionally different from long-term cultured parasites, especially in their invasion capabilities.
source: Our findings are consistent with another study investigating the impact of long-term culture (Mackinnon et al., 2009) which also found genes like merozoite surface proteins differentially expressed, however they were downregulated in long-term cultured parasites, whereas we found them upregulated in generation 1. This suggests that short-term cultured parasites might be transcriptionally different from long-term cultured parasites, especially in their invasion capabilities, something previously unobserved.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on comparison with a cited study.

claim: The similarity of the core transcriptomes of the in vitro samples compared to the heterogeneity seen in the ex vivo samples could be explained by a stress response upon entry to culture.
source: The similarity of the core transcriptomes of the in vitro samples compared to the heterogeneity seen in the ex vivo samples could be explained by a stress response upon entry to culture.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the PCA results.

claim: The marked differences presented suggest that the impact of short-term culture can override differences observed in both the in vivo core and var transcriptomes of different disease manifestations.
source: Critically, the marked differences presented here suggest that the impact of short-term culture can override differences observed in both the in vivo core and var transcriptomes of different disease manifestations.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the overall findings.

claim: Whilst var gene expression is often maintained, unpredictable switching does occur, necessitating that the similarity of in vivo and in vitro expression should be confirmed.
source: Whilst var gene expression is often maintained, unpredictable switching does occur, necessitating that the similarity of in vivo and in vitro expression should be confirmed.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the findings.

claim: The more extreme changes in the core transcriptome could have much bigger implications for understanding other aspects of parasite biology such as growth rates and drug susceptibility.
source: The more extreme changes in the core transcriptome could have much bigger implications for understanding other aspects of parasite biology such as growth rates and drug susceptibility and raise a need for additional caution.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation about the implications of the findings.
